summary: Vernon businesses can compare Michael McKerracher for hands-on design, content and practical marketing; Duford Digital for local websites and search strategy; Svice for defined website packages and marketing support; TheBomb for custom builds with hosting; and Vernon Software for packaged small-business websites. Choose by the scope and support your business needs.
takeaways: Decide whether you need a finished content service or can supply the material.
Check how the provider handles North Okanagan coverage and enquiries.
Compare recurring costs and account access before committing.

sections.body:
Michael McKerracher is a strong option for a Vernon owner who wants one collaborator to connect the website’s appearance, content and business purpose. I am based in Coldstream and work across the Okanagan on websites, marketing and systems that support the next customer action.

My portfolio includes local-service work for ABC Appliance and Cool Runnings, accommodation design for Okanagan Treehouse, and design and marketing for St. James School. Cool Runnings saw a 30% increase in qualified bookings after the connected website, SEO and conversion work.

Ask me about: improving an existing site, building useful service pages, training, ownership and making enquiries easier to handle. Scope and pricing are agreed for the project. See the selected website work.

Duford Digital is worth comparing when a Vernon business needs website work and local SEO considered together. Its North Okanagan service page shows professional, clinic and local-business examples and distinguishes template builds from custom projects.

Ask about: the service-area content your business actually needs, what is included at launch and what belongs in ongoing SEO. A company serving several towns should discuss real coverage and useful local differences before agreeing a page count. See Duford Digital’s Vernon services.

Svice is a useful option for a Vernon owner looking at a defined website package and related marketing services. Its published six-page offer asks the client to provide text, logos and images; its wider services include design, content, SEO and site management.

Ask about: how much material you will need to prepare and which writing or image work can be added. If you want a manageable launch, a defined scope can help, provided responsibilities are clear. Confirm editing access and support after the initial hosting period. Review Svice’s website offer.

TheBomb is relevant to a Vernon shortlist for a custom website with hosting and continuing support. Its public site presents custom design alongside SEO and maintenance services for businesses in the Okanagan and beyond.

Ask about: content development, the design review process and how updates will be handled after launch. If your business changes offers or seasonal information regularly, explain that before the platform and support arrangement are selected. Explore TheBomb’s services.

Vernon Software is worth considering when the owner prefers a packaged WordPress build. Its website service page describes small-business packages with a defined range of page counts and included setup features.

Ask about: content responsibilities, the package’s limits, integrations and ongoing maintenance. A starting price is useful only after you know whether the package covers the site your business needs. Clarify ownership and what future changes will cost. Review Vernon Software’s website packages.

A Vernon website proposal should make the work understandable to the owner who will use and maintain it. Bring a short brief describing the services, communities covered and the way customers book or enquire.

For a trade, ask how the site will distinguish the jobs you want from requests you cannot serve. For a practice, ask how a new client finds the right service and prepares for an appointment. For hospitality, ask how imagery, availability and booking details will connect.

  • Who writes and approves the service content?
  • Which account logins will the business control?
  • How are enquiries delivered and tested?
  • What training is included?
  • What are the ongoing costs and cancellation terms?

The Vernon business website guide provides a fuller brief. Use the cost checklist to compare the proposals against the same expectations.

faqs: Do I need a designer with an office in Vernon?

Not necessarily. Relevant work, clear communication and reliable support are important. If in-person meetings matter, confirm them directly. Michael McKerracher is based in nearby Coldstream and serves Vernon and the wider Okanagan.
Which option suits an owner who cannot write all the website copy?

Choose a proposal that explicitly includes interviews, page planning and writing. Michael McKerracher can include that work in the scope. For any package, check whether supplying text is your responsibility before comparing the price.
Can I start with a small site and add North Okanagan pages later?
Yes. Agree a structure and editing approach that can grow. Launch useful core pages first, then add local pages when you have distinct coverage details, relevant work or customer questions to answer.
